extractor: read directly from the official Department of Home Affairs page listed in source_roles
policy: Every entry quotes the official page it was read from. source_excerpt is verbatim Department of Home Affairs wording in the Department's own casing. immi.homeaffairs.gov.au renders its visa content client-side; the wording quoted here is the page content as published in the page's own content payload, which is what a reader sees in a browser. Nothing here is paraphrased into a requirement, and nothing is included that the page did not state. Australia publishes no application form identifier for this visa - the application is made online in ImmiAccount - so official_form_code is null throughout.
not_extracted: THIN SOURCE. Only the subclass 482 landing page could be read, and that page carries a short summary of the eligibility criteria rather than the full criteria. The registered 'eligibility' source (https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/visas/getting-a-visa/visa-listing/skills-in-demand-visa-subclass-482/core-skills-stream) - which holds the per-stream criteria, evidence, steps and English language thresholds - was NOT read: immi.homeaffairs.gov.au returned HTTP 403 to the source monitor on this run and the rule is never to retry through a 403. This file is therefore a floor, not a complete picture of the subclass 482 requirements.

STREAM SCOPE. Subclass 482 has multiple streams (including the Core Skills stream registered as this entry's eligibility source). The three criteria recorded below come from the subclass-level landing page and are stated by the Department for the subclass, not for one stream. No stream-specific requirement is recorded.
The landing page's 'warning' slot contains unpublished CMS placeholder text ('Warning text here. Anchor with information here') rather than a real Departmental warning. It is ignored.
The registered 'forms' source (https://online.immi.gov.au/lusc/login) is disallowed by that host's robots.txt ('User-agent: * / Disallow: /'). It was not fetched and nothing is quoted from it.

Fees / visa application charge. The registered fees source (https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/visas/getting-a-visa/fees-and-charges/current-visa-pricing) renders its whole price table client-side from an API; the served HTML contains only the column headings ('Base application charge', 'Additional applicant charge 18 and over', 'Additional applicant charge under 18', 'Non-internet application charge', 'Subsequent temporary application charge') and no amounts. No amount and no currency was stated, so no fee is recorded.
Page 'last updated' date. Rendered client-side and absent from the served HTML, so page_dates is empty.

requirements.label: Be nominated for a skilled position by an approved sponsor
requirements.description: The Department describes the visa as one that lets an employer sponsor a suitably skilled worker to fill a position they cannot find a suitably skilled Australian to fill.
requirements.source_excerpt: You must: be nominated for a skilled position by an approved sponsor

requirements.label: Have the right skills to do the job
requirements.description: The landing page states this at subclass level and does not state how the skills are assessed. The stream page that would say more could not be read.
requirements.source_excerpt: You must: have the right skills to do the job

requirements.label: Meet the relevant English language requirements
requirements.description: The landing page states the requirement exists but states no test, score or exemption. Those are on the stream page, which could not be read.
requirements.source_excerpt: You must: meet the relevant English language requirements
